outcome: Since 26 January 2024 the full Brennan conjecture remains open, but several restricted cases have been settled: Aleman and Kouroupis (2024/2025) proved it for continuous semigroups of holomorphic functions; Jin (2025/2026) proved it for all univalent rational functions in the unit disk; and Zheng (2026) proved it for basins of attraction at infinity of certain monic polynomials. No AI system was involved in any of this work.
summary: The frozen-revision statement asks for a resolution of Brennan's conjecture: estimating the integral of |F'|^p over certain domains for conformal maps F onto the unit disk, for p in (4/3, 4). Wikipedia's own article (checked 2026-09-22) has not been updated and still reports the pre-2024 state: Brennan's original range 4/3<p<p0, Bertilsson's 1999 extension to 4/3<p<3.422, and 'the full result remains open' (the Hedenmalm-Shimorin improvement to p<3.75 is also pre-2024 and not part of this window). Three genuine cases of the conjecture were settled in the window, all confirming it (no case has been found false): (1) Aleman & Kouroupis, arXiv:2409.15074 (submitted 2024-09-23, revised 2025-04-14), prove the conjecture in full (all p in the stated range) for the restricted class of domains arising as images of continuous semigroups of holomorphic self-maps of the disk -- read via WebFetch, confirmed no AI/ML mentioned, uses classical complex analysis plus Bekolle-Bonami weight and integration-operator spectrum results. (2) Jin, arXiv:2512.09330 (first submitted 2025-12-10, 13 revisions through 2026-06), as a corollary of determining the exact integral means spectrum of all univalent rational functions on the disk, proves the conjecture holds for that entire class -- abstract fetched directly, no AI/ML mentioned, purely analytic/Teichmuller-theoretic methods. (3) Zheng, arXiv:2604.12240 (submitted 2026-04-14), proves the conjecture for basins of attraction at infinity of a broad class of monic polynomials z^m+a0 (m>=3) and polynomials with small non-leading coefficients, extending a known result of Baranski-Volberg-Zdunik -- these basins are simply-connected domains admitting a conformal map to the disk, so this is a restriction to a class of domains rather than a change of the question, though the framing in terms of dynamical basins rather than 'certain subsets' as worded on Wikipedia makes the classification a judgment call. None of the three papers mentions any AI system, machine learning, or computer-assisted search; all are traditional human proofs verified by classical complex-analytic argument. No AI-related result of any kind (generated proof, assisted argument, bound-moving computation, or withdrawn claim) was found for this problem in the window. I did not find any paper claiming or retracting a full proof of the general conjecture, nor any record-style or numerical result that would change status further. Status is 'partial' because multiple genuine cases were settled (all confirming the conjecture, hence resolution_direction 'confirmed'), while the general conjecture as stated remains open.
competing_reading: The Zheng basin-of-attraction paper could instead be read as a related/variant problem rather than a case: Brennan's conjecture is normally stated for domains arising from conformal Riemann mapping theory (quasidisks, Julia-set complements already studied by Baranski-Volberg-Zdunik), and one could argue that framing it dynamically (via polynomial iteration) changes the question's flavor even though the underlying object -- a simply-connected domain mapped conformally to the disk -- is unchanged. If read as a variant, only the Aleman-Kouroupis and Jin papers count as cases, and the status conclusion (partial, confirmed) is unaffected either way since both of those are unambiguous cases.
what_would_settle_it: A published taxonomy from Brennan-conjecture specialists (e.g. a survey or the next edition of Pommerenke-style geometric function theory literature) explicitly listing basin-of-attraction domains as an instance of 'certain subsets' in Brennan's original conjecture, versus treating dynamically-defined domains as a separate research thread.

events.what: Aleman and Kouroupis prove Brennan's conjecture for domains that are images of continuous semigroups of holomorphic self-maps of the disk
Jin determines the integral means spectrum of univalent rational functions on the disk, giving Brennan's conjecture for that class
events.credibility_reason: 13 revisions within about six months suggests the argument has been patched repeatedly; no identified error, and the author works in the area.

events.what: Zheng proves Brennan's conjecture for basins of attraction at infinity of certain monic polynomials

judgement.doubts: All three events are restrictions to classes of simply connected domains, so each is a case; the Zheng basins are still simply connected domains mapped conformally, so the record's 'variant' worry does not apply. None is a full proof. Status, AI role and direction all agree with the record. Jin's many revisions are a mild doubt only.
